subject: Request: Limited EU transfer exception & DPA clause alignment for Novamed pilot
messages:
From: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@novamed.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: 2028-08-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: Pilot data flow – limited EU transfer exception request + DPA redlines

Hi Hannah / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the pilot is live next month and we have one sticking point before procurement will sign: our security team requires that for the first 90 days of pilot activity we keep primary patient identifiers in the EU, but Novamed needs the hosted inference calls to hit Redwood’s us-east endpoint for latency reasons.

We prepared a short request and attached our DPA redline (Novamed_DPA_Redline_v1.docx). High level: we would like a temporary, narrowly-scoped transfer exception tied to pilot traffic only, with defined compensating controls and daily audit logging.

Quick asks:
- Can Redwood confirm whether a 90-day pilot exception is operationally feasible?
- If feasible, can you propose exact wording we can fold into the Order Form (transfer exception addendum)?
- We need an internal timeline — procurement wants signoff by next Friday (2028-09-08).

Attachment: Novamed_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (redline of Redwood DPA)

Thanks — feel free to loop in whoever you need.

Claire Jensen
Director, Regulatory Affairs | Novamed
claire.jensen@novamed.com
+44 20 5555 1212
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@novamed.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-30T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot data flow – limited EU transfer exception request + DPA redlines

Thanks Claire — looping in Legal (Ben) and Engineering (Irene) to scope operational feasibility and draft language. Initial notes:

- We want to avoid permanent Order Form changes; a 90-day pilot addendum is reasonable in principle if we can demonstrate strong technical safeguards.
- Need to confirm whether prefix routing + KV caching can be isolated to EU-only for identifiers while allowing model inference in us-east for compute.
- Please confirm whether Novamed considers pseudonymization sufficient for those identifiers during transit/processing.

Ben / Irene — can you triage the attached redline and propose: (1) an Order Form addendum paragraph, and (2) required compensating controls (logging, retention windows, access limits) we can promise in writing?

I’ll hold an internal sync tomorrow 09:30 PDT to finalize the draft before sharing with Claire & procurement.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Manager, Customer Privacy & Contracts | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-30T14:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot data flow – limited EU transfer exception request + DPA redlines

Hannah / team,

Reviewing Novamed_DPA_Redline_v1.docx — good catch on the transfer language. Proposed path:

1) Temporary Transfer Exception Addendum (90 days) — draft language (high level):
   - Scope: applies only to pilot traffic defined in Order Form Annex A (traffic tagged as "novamed-pilot-<id>").
   - Duration: 90 days from go-live, non-renewing except by mutual written amendment.
   - Controls: (i) Pseudonymization of direct identifiers prior to export; (ii) daily audit log of access and cross-border requests retained for 180 days; (iii) emergency escalation contact and 24h response SLA for data incidents.

2) DPA redline comments: we will accept Novamed’s deletion/return obligations but push back on their proposed blanket restriction that prohibits temporary compute outside the EEA — instead we offer the pilot exception plus low-risk mitigations.

3) Commercial / Order Form: mark transfer exception as "no-charge" for pilot but note possible surcharge if pilot converts to production requiring persistent routing guarantees.

I attached a short memo (redline_notes_by_Redwood.docx) with exact wording and two alternative clause options (one narrower, one with stronger logging).

Risk note: if Novamed refuses both exception and our conditional mitigations, legal will need to escalate to Sales leadership (possible delay to go-live).

Ben Carter
Lead Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redline_notes_by_Redwood.docx
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-31T08:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot data flow – limited EU transfer exception request + DPA redlines

Ben / team, quick operational feasibility from infra:

- We can tag pilot requests at the client SDK layer (header: X-Client-Flow: novamed-pilot-7843). That enables request routing rules in the gateway.
- Option A (preferred): pseudonymize identifiers at the SDK (Novamed side) before sending to Redwood — zero EU export. Needs a small SDK change (1 sprint) and coordination with Novamed devs.
- Option B: allow inference in us-east but use prefix/KV cache isolation and an ephemeral token that limits access to model outputs only. We'll also enable enhanced audit logging (daily export to an EU-hosted S3 bucket) and a retention window of 30 days.

Operational asks for Novamed:
- Confirm whether they can accept pseudonymization (Option A) during pilot. If not, Option B is doable but requires:
  * Signed transfer exception addendum;
  * Access controls (role-based) with RBAC proof (list of Redwood staff with access);
  * Audit log export to EU for the duration.

I’ll prepare a short runbook and the specific header schema for the SDK by EOD today; can share to Claire’s team.

Irene Choi
Principal Engineer, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@novamed.com>, Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-31T11:50:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot data flow – limited EU transfer exception request + DPA redlines

Claire / procurement team — thanks for the prompt submission. Redwood’s internal recommendation is the following combined approach for the pilot:

- Implement Option A where possible (pseudonymization at SDK). If Novamed cannot modify the SDK for this pilot, proceed with Option B plus the Transfer Exception Addendum below.

Draft Transfer Exception Addendum (summary):
- Applies only to pilot-flagged traffic, expires 90 days after go-live, non-renewable without mutual written consent.
- Compensating controls: EU audit-log export (daily), 30-day retention for pilot logs, RBAC listing for staff with access, 24-hour incident contact and response SLA.
- No change to broader DPA obligations — this is a narrowly-tailored operational exception limited to the pilot ID.

Commercial note: we will not charge for the pilot exception. If Novamed requests a permanent cross-border routing guarantee after pilot, we will need to revisit pricing and infra commitments.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
1) Novamed confirms preferred option (A or B) by 2028-09-04.
2) Redwood sends final addendum language and runbook by 2028-09-05.
3) Procurement executes by 2028-09-08 to keep the current go-live.

Please confirm and let us know if you want the drafted addendum pushed into DocuSign now.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts & Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@novamed.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>, Dawn Lee <dawn.lee@novamed.com>
Date: 2028-09-01T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot data flow – limited EU transfer exception request + DPA redlines

Laura / Hannah — thanks, this is helpful. Novamed prefers Option B for this pilot (we cannot ship an SDK change in time). Procurement is comfortable with a 90-day exception provided the audit-log export and RBAC list are included.

We are ready to sign the addendum — please send the DocuSign envelope and we’ll aim to execute by 2028-09-07. For reference I’ve pasted Ben’s proposed summary below.
